# Execution plan template: replace with one approved outcome

This is a template, not a live initiative. Copy only when a plan is needed, choose the next unused number, and follow [the plan lifecycle](../plans/README.md). Replace instructions with concise task-specific facts; do not pre-check work.

Lifecycle: proposed
Approval: not granted
Verification: not run
Release: not released

## Purpose / Big Picture

Describe the observable user outcome and explicit non-goals. Link the owning feature and distinguish approved scope from unresolved decisions.

## Progress

- [ ] Establish current state and scoped authorization.
- [ ] Complete the approved outcome and its verification.
- [ ] Update owning documentation, evidence, and closure disposition.

Replace this example checklist with real milestones. Include dates/results only when known.

## Surprises & Discoveries

Record actual discoveries and their evidence as they occur. Say none recorded initially.

## Decision Log

Record the decision, reason, alternatives when useful, scope/approval source, and date. Do not invent approval from a draft document.

## Outcomes & Retrospective

Record what works, what was verified, remaining limitations, and release disposition. Initially state that no implementation outcome is established.

## Context and Orientation

Name the current branch/revision, relevant architecture/feature owners, stable code entry points, neighboring features, and existing tests. Include only context needed to resume this task.

## Plan of Work

Describe the smallest coherent changes and expected affected paths. Keep permanent behavior in the owning feature and update this plan as actual paths differ.

## Concrete Steps

Give exact commands/procedures using the supported runtime and safe test data. Distinguish intended commands from executed results; do not invent unavailable tools.

## Validation and Acceptance

List observable success, relevant permission/privacy/retry/failure checks, and required browser/provider/database coverage. Specify what constitutes a blocker versus an explicitly accepted limitation.

## Idempotence and Recovery

Explain safe retries, interruption, rollback/forward recovery, and protection of real data. No destructive shared-environment action is authorized by a template.

## Artifacts and Notes

Record actual revision/date, environment, commands, outcomes, omissions, and sanitized evidence locations as work occurs. Never include real tokens or private customer content.

## Interfaces and Dependencies

Name existing contracts/packages/services and justify any necessary additions. Avoid hypothetical abstractions. Before closure add `Closed: YYYY-MM-DD` and a meaningful `Closure:` summary under the plan standard.
